scope: 31 supplied historical table cases, plus bounded contextual corrections. Research only.
method: Primary issuer announcements, financial statements, transaction-adviser first-hand notices and court records. Mirrors/syndications identified explicitly. Announcements alone are not treated as closing evidence. Dates labelled by meaning; a reporting bound is not an exact closing date. Source descriptions, HQs, valuation superlatives and forecasts are preserved in original_claim but not comprehensively independently verified.

status_definitions.completed: Explicit completion/effective acquisition date in primary source.
status_definitions.completed_reported: Primary source explicitly reports acquired/completed or records acquisition retrospectively; date precision separately qualified.
status_definitions.announced_acquisition: Primary announcement found; exact closing or completion independently unverified.
status_definitions.acquisition_reported_by_transaction_advi: First-hand deal adviser statement, without separately dated corporate closing notice.
status_definitions.not_verified_as_completed_different_buye: Supplied buyer completion unverified; later primary buyer evidence requires correction/uncertainty label.
status_definitions.not_completed_as_claimed_contested_closi: Court evidence contradicts presentation as an uncomplicated completed acquisition.

contextual_examples.title: Google / NASA and Google Maps
contextual_examples.original_claim: E.g. Golden Harvest JV with Village Roadshow to form Golden Village and Google JV with NASA to form Google Maps
contextual_examples.correction: Google dates Maps launch to February 8, 2005. NASA describes later research collaborations and planetary content for Google Moon/Earth. Replace the claim that Google and NASA formed Google Maps with a correctly sourced R&D collaboration example.

primary_sources.title: A look back at 15 years of mapping the world
NASA / Google agreements library
Astrogram June 2008: NASA, Google announce lease at Ames Research Center

contextual_examples.limits_uncertainty: NASA’s 2006 newsletter loosely uses joint venture for collaboration; that does not establish a jointly owned company or Maps origin. Do not replace it with an unsourced corporate JV legal classification.

contextual_examples.title: Apple / Beats price and vertical-merger classification
contextual_examples.original_claim: E.g. Apple Buys Dr Dre Beats Electronics for $3.2Bn in 2014
contextual_examples.correction: Apple’s May 28, 2014 agreement announced $3.0bn total: approximately $2.6bn purchase price plus $0.4bn vesting over time, for Beats Music and Beats Electronics. The supplied $3.2bn figure does not match that announcement.

primary_sources.title: Apple to Acquire Beats Music & Beats Electronics

contextual_examples.limits_uncertainty: This is agreement-stage evidence, not a closing notice. Complementary audio hardware and music services alone do not prove the source’s production-chain definition of vertical merger; label strategic acquisition rather than force a structural category.

contextual_examples.title: Tata / Jaguar Land Rover conglomerate classification
contextual_examples.original_claim: E.g. Tata Group acquired Jaguar-Land Rover in 2008 from Ford for $2.3Bn
contextual_examples.correction: Tata Motors, an automotive manufacturer, completed its purchase of Jaguar Land Rover businesses from Ford on June 2, 2008 for $2.3bn net consideration on a cash-free debt-free basis. Use the actual automotive buyer rather than diversified Tata Group to justify an unrelated-industry example.

primary_sources.title: Tata Motors Completes Acquisition Of Jaguar Land Rover
8-K, Item 2.01, Completion of disposition

contextual_examples.limits_uncertainty: Classification is an inference from buyer and target activities. Do not assert a uniquely authoritative merger taxonomy from the announcement.

contextual_examples.title: AIG rescue as LBO example
contextual_examples.correction: Government assistance began in September 2008 and was expanded/restructured in 2008–2009. GAO records up to $182.3bn made available, not a single 2008 buyout price.

primary_sources.title: Financial Crisis: Review of Federal Reserve System Financial Assistance to AIG, GAO-11-616

primary_sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
primary_sources.title: Actions Related to AIG

contextual_examples.limits_uncertainty: Committed assistance differs from disbursed funds, acquisition consideration and net fiscal cost. Sources establish rescue financing, not a conventional leveraged sponsor buyout.

contextual_examples.title: JAL rescue as LBO example
contextual_examples.correction: JAL entered corporate reorganisation and received ETIC support in January 2010. JAL subsequently records a ¥350bn ETIC capital injection after bankruptcy. The supplied US$11bn needs a defined funding perimeter and dated exchange rate.

primary_sources.title: JAL Received Decision on Support from ETIC and the Court’s Decision on Commencement of Corporate Reorganization Proceedings
Regular Press Conference (September 18, 2013)

contextual_examples.limits_uncertainty: Do not equate capital injection, total support and debt relief. Bounded primary review does not verify the supplied dollar total or conventional LBO classification.

contextual_examples.title: MAS recovery plan as LBO example
contextual_examples.correction: Khazanah’s August 29, 2014 recovery plan provided up to RM6bn further investment, conditional and staggered. Present as rescue, delisting and restructuring context rather than an established leveraged sponsor buyout.

primary_sources.title: Annual Review 2014: MAS Recovery Plan case study

contextual_examples.limits_uncertainty: The ceiling is not a claim that RM6bn was disbursed immediately or entirely used to buy shares. Full capital-structure review was outside this bounded check.

contextual_examples.title: SIA pandemic recapitalisation as LBO example
contextual_examples.correction: SIA’s March 26, 2020 plan offered S$5.3bn rights equity and up to S$9.7bn mandatory convertible bonds, plus a S$4bn bridge facility. June 8 release confirms S$8.8bn rights issue completed June 5 and about S$10bn fresh liquidity including credit facilities. The supplied S$16bn is not supported as a single rescue or buyout amount.

primary_sources.title: Singapore Airlines To Issue S$5.3 Billion In New Equity And Raise Up To S$9.7 Billion Via Mandatory Convertible Bonds
Singapore Airlines Secures S$10 Billion In Fresh Liquidity

contextual_examples.limits_uncertainty: Separate announced facilities, issued securities, available credit and actual proceeds. This recapitalisation does not establish an LBO or privatisation.

priority_corrections: finAPI/Yapily is not verified completed; primary target confirms Fabrick 75% purchase reported June 18, 2025.
Reby/House of Lithium must retain failed/contested closing context, based on court opinion.
Side buyer should be Randstad France/group, not Innovation Fund.
Clicars 2022 was remaining minority stake after earlier control.
ProGlove and iFollow refer to majority stakes, not proven 100% purchases.
Apple Beats agreed amount $3bn; NASA collaboration did not create Google Maps; rescue financing is not automatically an LBO.
